newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits little changed in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits little changed in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were little changed in featureless trade, dealers said on Friday.
They said most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. October import/export and Federal Budget data.
U.S. import and export prices for October are due at 1500 GMT. In September, import prices rose 0.8 percent but export prices fell 0.8 percent.
The Federal Budget for October is forecast to have narrowed to US$32 billion compared with September's $35.37 billion.

"The market was quiet and featureless in the morning due mainly to an absence of fresh incentives. Some people are waiting for possible direction from tonight's release of the import/export and federal budget numbers," a local dealer said.
"But I don't think there will be much impact here as the numbers have been into the market and most people have squared or are squaring their positions ahead of the weekend," he said.
In day-to-day rates, weekend, Monday/Tuesday and week-fixed were unchanged from Thursday's common 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent, respectively.
Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged at 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent, three-months unchanged at 5-1/2 5-3/8, nine-months unchanged at 5-9/16 5-7/16 and twelve-months unchanged at 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent.
